rev.summary:
I found one blocking issue in fix2-campaigns (1b320a9) and several should-fix gaps; most of the fixes work. Backend tests pass: test_campaigns, test_rest_broadcasts, test_deletion, test_portraits and test_surface (246 passed), plus test_account, test_auth, test_users, test_ws_circle, test_access and test_ws_gm_view (709 passed). The frontend builds and the commit has no em dashes. I checked in Chromium at 1440x900, 1366x768 and 390x844. The join-request card shows "from <username>" with the oxblood flags. The invite slip names the living investigator, and the Activity Log gets the invite line. After a retire, the released investigator shows under Not in a campaign once the Case Ledger opens, and the desk of the released investigator goes to the hub with a notice.

Blocking: campaign_retired is now sent with broadcast_users to every socket of the owners. A player playing campaign A, who entered through the Last Played tome, is thrown off that desk to the hub with a wrong notice when campaign B, where they also have an investigator, is retired. The campaign check lets it through because the auto-filled lastPlayedCampaign has no campaignId. I reproduced this; screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/rev8512/shots/13_other_campaign_desk_after_retire.png.

Should fix:
- owner_username is missing from the investigator_rejected and rejoin frames, so on a second Lightkeeper tab the labels and flags vanish (screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/rev8512/shots/02_after_reject_elsewhere.png).
- A player's Last Played tome still names the retired campaign and opens the desk under it.
- The owner of a dead investigator is told it is "free to join another".
- Usernames, which are login names, now go to every member.
- WEBSOCKET.md is not updated for the new activity_log sources or the new payload field.
- The player is still not warned that rejoining retires their living investigator.

All temporary servers were stopped and both databases dropped. Nothing in the worktree was changed.

issues.problem: campaign_retired is sent with manager.broadcast_users(owners), which reaches every socket of those users on any channel. The player handler (frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:1108) relies on isForThisCampaign, which returns true when activeCampaignId() is null. That is the case after the hub's auto Last Played (useAutoLastPlayed sets no campaignId) and after a reload of that state. Reproduced on 8512: a player with Alma in 'Kept Case' (entered via the Last Played tome) and Bea in 'Doomed Case'. Retiring Doomed Case threw them off Alma's desk to the hub with 'The Lightkeeper retired the campaign. Your investigator is free to join another.' (shots/13_other_campaign_desk_after_retire.png). A GM desk the player runs elsewhere and sockets on other characters are exposed to the same path.

The 'released' list is already built and unused; add the dead ones too if their owners should hear it. A message reaching both a character key and broadcast_users is not needed. Alternatively, put the character ids in the payload and have the handler act only when socketGameId is one of them. Add a test: a socket of the same user on a character in another campaign gets nothing.

issues.problem: owner_username is only in GET roster and investigator_joined. investigator_rejected's pending_investigators (get_char_dict) and the rejoin's investigator_approved/character_joined_mid_campaign cards lack it, and the store replaces the lists with them. issues.problem: The module-level keptDraft is restored on every remount, even when it is not a draft at all but simply the dispatch that was on the desks. The circle sync effects now skip mount, so a dispatch or End Assignment that arrives while the letter is unmounted (Map, Notebook or Circle open) is never shown on the letter. I reproduced it in Chromium (1440x900, API 8515). Tab A dispatches 'The old mill' and opens Map. A second tab of the same Lightkeeper dispatches 'The docks', then closes. Tab A presses 'Use this tab' and goes back to Roster. The letter still reads 'The old mill' / 'Meet at dusk.' and says 'NOT DISPATCHED YET', while the circle and the players' desks hold 'The docks' (out_8515/e2_tabA_roster.png in my scratch run). Before this change the letter showed 'The docks'. One press of Dispatch now silently puts the old dispatch back over the new one on every player's desk. This is also inconsistent with a mounted letter, where an arriving dispatch overwrites the draft. Same on a phone or a second device.
issues.fix: Keep the circle values the draft was based on next to it, e.g. keptDraft = { circleId, base: {location, atmosphere, dispatch_text}, location, atmosphere, ownText }. On mount, use the kept draft only when the circle's current location, atmosphere and dispatch_text still equal kept.base; otherwise seed from the circle, as a mounted letter would. A simpler alternative: keep the draft only while it differs from the circle values, and clear keptDraft when a dispatch arrives with values different from the base.

issues.problem: The new paragraph sits under '### How does the notebook work?', but it covers three things that are not the notebook: the Pass Notes recipients, the dispatch draft and the timer's screen-reader status. Nobody looking up pass notes, the dispatch or the timer would find them there.
issues.fix: Put the Pass Notes rule in a chat or pass-notes place of its own (e.g. a short '### Who reads a passed note?' or a bullet in the Lightkeeper/desks section). Move the dispatch-draft and timer lines into '## What the Lightkeeper's changes look like on the players' desks', or into the dispatch and timer bullets there.

issues.problem: The 'skip on mount' guard is a ref set in a mount effect. Under React.StrictMode (on in src/main.jsx) development builds run effects twice. On the second run mounted.current is already true, so the three sync effects overwrite the restored draft with the circle values on every remount. Under `npm run dev` the fix therefore looks broken, and the next developer could easily 'fix' it the wrong way. Production builds are not affected.
issues.fix: Decide on mount by comparing values rather than by a mount flag: track the previous circle values in a ref initialised to the current ones, and sync only when circle.location, atmosphere or dispatch_text actually differs from that ref. Doing this together with the blocking fix's base comparison makes it StrictMode-safe.

issues.problem: A character named 'Lightkeeper' (the server now reserves the name) appears in other players' lists as '@Lightkeeper (and the Lightkeeper)' with the value '@Lightkeeper'. That duplicates the '@Lightkeeper only' option's value, so TargetDropdown gets a duplicate React key and both options send to the Lightkeeper alone.

rev.summary: Three of the four items are correct and I confirmed them in Chromium: the Pass Notes recipients (phone, tablet and the Lightkeeper's desk, plus routing), the timer status after Reset (both desks), and the hub tack removal. The dispatch draft fix works for a plain section switch but brings a regression. The module-level draft is restored on remount even when it was just the last sent dispatch, and the mount-skipping sync effects ignore changes that arrived meanwhile. I reproduced it with a second tab: after another tab dispatched 'The docks', the first tab's letter showed the old 'The old mill' and 'NOT DISPATCHED YET', one press away from overwriting the players' dispatch. That should be fixed before merge by restoring the draft only when the circle values it was based on are unchanged. The FAQ paragraph is also misplaced under the notebook heading. Backend: test_ws_chat_notebook.py and test_surface.py, 68 passed on a throwaway database (dropped). Frontend build passes. Servers on 8515/4515 were stopped by PID and fix_desk_8515 was dropped. Nothing in the worktree was edited.

issues.problem: The log pins to its foot only when logEntries.length changes. The store keeps 50 lines (gameStore.js:178, LOG_LINES = 50), and a reload is sent up to 100 lines of history (manager.py:55), so any session past 50 lines has a fixed length and new lines stop pinning. The new atFoot/ResizeObserver code only helps when the box changes size. Checked in Chromium at 1366x768 with 60 lines seeded: four of Iris's rolls arrived on Bram's desk and the gap to the end grew 24, 48, 72, 96 px, with the newest roll out of view (screenshot cap_iris.png). Bram's own second roll, with the slip already up, was also left 24 px short and hidden. This is the item's symptom ('the roll just made is hidden below the box') on a path every real session reaches.
issues.fix: Re-run the pin on the newest entry as well as the count, e.g. key the effect on logEntries[logEntries.length - 1] (or on logEntries itself) and scroll when atFoot.current is true. Or watch the content with a MutationObserver/ResizeObserver on the list. Then recheck at the 50-line cap with another seat's rolls and with your own rolls while the slip is up.

issues.problem: The sticky footer does not stick at the dialog's bottom edge. Chromium insets the sticky area by the scroller's padding, so with bottom-0 the footer stops 20px (sm: 32px) above the inner bottom edge, and the pick cards scroll by, visibly and tappably, in the band under Confirm and Later. Measured at 390x705 with two picks ticked: inner bottom 668, footer bottom 648, and elementFromPoint 5px above the edge hits a pick label (screenshot a10_peek.png shows 'Gild an additional action' under the buttons). Only the fully scrolled end looks flush, which is what the implementer's screenshot showed. ScarModal.jsx:241 has the same 20px band (inner 685, footer 665).
issues.fix: Give both footers a bottom offset equal to the negative padding (-bottom-5 sm:-bottom-8 with the existing -mb), or use the verifier's structure: panel flex flex-col with max-h, content in a min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto body, footer shrink-0 outside the scroller.

issues.problem: When the Lightkeeper sends update_drive for a member (the server allows it, and the implementer's choices say the line covers her case), the line still reads '<member> set Nerve to 2 of 3.', so the player is named as the one who did it. Other handlers say 'The Lightkeeper dealt X a mark' when ctx.is_gm (marks.py:375), and the first report asked for 'The Lightkeeper set Latch's Nerve to 2 of 4'. It also writes a campaign-wide line naming a character that is still pending approval (the case in test_access.py:299).
issues.fix: When ctx.is_gm, log f"The Lightkeeper set {character.name}'s {Pool} to {value} of {maximum}.". Add a test for the Lightkeeper's wording next to test_gm_may_set_a_members_drive_but_not_an_outsiders, and consider skipping the line for a character that is not yet approved.

issues.problem: The item is only partly fixed. The triage's expected result and the first report both say the Lightkeeper can set a drive from her copy of the sheet. The implementer skipped this, so her copy still has 0 live pips. The server already accepts update_drive from her, and traumaEdit already carries setMarks and setScars for exactly this kind of correction.
issues.fix: Add traumaEdit.setDrive(pool, value), sending update_drive with character_id, and make the dossier's pips live (refill and clear the last pip) when editing is on in the Lightkeeper's trauma edit. If this is deliberately deferred, record it as a known gap rather than calling the item fixed.

issues.problem: The new waiting strip has a border-2 border-candle-gold. DESIGN.md (Candle Gold) says gold 'is not used for headings, labels or borders that are not gilded or selected'. This strip is neither.
issues.fix: Use a border the palette allows for a notice, e.g. border-sepia or border-ink, matching the scar strip's pattern (that one uses oxblood).

issues.problem: basis-40 (160px) plus the Vote button no longer fits on a 390 phone, so every row, even a short name like 'The Harrow Watch', now puts Vote on its own line above the name. At 360 a lone count chip also wraps onto a third line by itself. Nothing is clipped and the leading row reads well (checked at 390, 360 and 320), but every row is now two or three lines tall in papers that are already a long scroll on a phone.
issues.fix: Use a smaller basis (e.g. basis-24 or basis-28), or keep Vote and the name in one nowrap group and let only the tags wrap.

issues.problem: The new clear pip sits 2px from the refill pip and both are 20x20 on a phone (measured x 170 and 192). A finger that misses the refill now clears a point instead. It can be undone and the pip size is not new, but DESIGN.md asks for 44px touch targets.
issues.fix: Give the live pips a 44px hit area on touch screens without changing their drawn size, the way .touch-pip does for the Illumination dots.

issues.problem: After Later or Escape, focus falls to the page body (measured: activeElement BODY), so keyboard and screen-reader users have to find the new strip. The regress agent noted this too.
issues.fix: After dismissing, focus the strip's 'Choose advancements (N)' button, or let useDialog return focus there.

issues.problem: In the action row this change touched, Decide later is 40px tall and Record scar 36px, both under the 44px touch rule. This was already so before the change.
issues.fix: Add [@media(pointer:coarse)]:min-h-[44px] to both buttons while the row is being edited.

Clearing the last pip goes 2->1, a double click stops at 0 with no duplicate line, refill 0->3 and keyboard Enter both work, the values survive a reload, and the line appears on Bram's, Iris's and the Lightkeeper's logs. Still missing: the Lightkeeper's copy has no drive editing (skipped, but part of the expected result), and a drive the Lightkeeper sets is logged under the player's name.

phone-dialog-buttons-below-fold: at 390x705, Confirm and Later, and Decide later and Record scar, stay in view and tappable with the sub-pickers open or text typed. But the sticky footer stops 20px above the dialog's bottom edge, so content scrolls by under the buttons. The formation papers' jump list was skipped as agreed.
rev.summary:
I reviewed fix2-player (f5e8fcd against 63d80f4) and made no edits. Backend tests pass: test_ws_character, test_access, test_ws_gm_view and test_surface (491), plus test_ws_connect and test_ws_rolls (232), which also send update_drive and which the implementer had not run, all on throwaway databases that I dropped afterwards. The Vite build passes. No em dashes, and the commit trailer is correct.

In Chromium (API on 8516, preview on 4516, my own database) I checked the five screens:
- **Drive pips:** they now clear and log. The player path works on laptop and phone, and the line reaches every desk.
- **Advancement way back:** the strip replaces the floating button and works on phone, laptop and 1920.
- **Leading name row:** it no longer collapses at 390, 360 or 320.
- **Phone dialogs:** the buttons in both dialogs stay in view on a phone.

Problems found:
- **Blocking:** the Activity Log still loses its newest line once the store's 50-line cap is reached, because the pin is keyed on the entry count. I reproduced it with 60 lines: other players' rolls drifted 24 to 96px out of view, and an own roll was hidden by 24px.
- **Should:**
  - Both sticky footers stop 20px above the dialog's bottom edge, and content scrolls by under the buttons.
  - A drive the Lightkeeper sets is logged under the player's name.
  - The Lightkeeper's copy of the sheet still cannot set a drive. This was skipped, but it is in the item's expected result.
  - The new strip's gold border breaks the DESIGN.md Candle Gold rule.
- **Nits:** name rows now put Vote on its own line on phones; the drive pips and the scar dialog's buttons are under the 44px touch size; focus is left on the page body after Later.

All servers were stopped by PID, the databases dropped, and the worktree is clean. My scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-TTRPG-VTT-CO/29eccd1d-b7aa-5d30-ac75-eae521bfb965/scratchpad/rv (shots/cap_iris.png, a10_peek.png, s04_peek.png, n_390.png, a07_desktop_strip.png).

choices: Log pin keyed on the newest entry object plus the count, so a reader scrolled up is still taken to the foot by a new line, as before.
Lightkeeper drive line: 'The Lightkeeper set <name>'s Nerve to 2 of 3.' No line for a character that is not active (pending approval).
The Lightkeeper's drive pips go live only while the dossier's trauma Edit toggle is on; setDrive updates the local sheet at once like setMarks.
Waiting strip border is sepia, not oxblood, so it differs from the scar strip but stays inside the palette rules.
Sticky footers use -bottom-5 sm:-bottom-8, the existing negative padding, rather than restructuring the dialog into a flex column.
Name rows in the formation papers use basis-28 so Vote and a short name fit one line on a 390px phone.
No new text in FAQ.md or DESIGN.md; only WEBSOCKET.md changed.
